content.value_statement: Data element strategies often rely on fragmented evidence and inflated market claims. This skill structures maturity, competition, opportunities, and sizing with explicit assumptions.
actual_capabilities: Maps the market across element, circulation, service, application, and infrastructure layers.
Assesses market maturity using policy, transaction, financing, technology, and adoption signals.
Compares competitors by positioning, customers, cases, pricing models, strengths, and weaknesses.
Evaluates business models through repeat customers, positive gross margin, and replicability.
Estimates market size with top-down and bottom-up methods, assumptions, and cross-checks.
Produces opportunity lists, trend reports, case studies, strategic inputs, and customer materials.
limitations: The knowledge base mainly covers China's market and requires external sources for international comparisons.
The skill has no built-in live data feed and may not reflect events after its reference date.
Market estimates depend on user inputs, source quality, definitions, and assumptions.
Outputs are analytical guidance, not legal, regulatory, accounting, or investment advice.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Growth Opportunities
use_cases.description: Rank service, industry, circulation, and financialization opportunities against capabilities, timing, evidence, and execution barriers.

use_cases.title: Validate a Business Model
use_cases.description: Test a proposed data service using repeat demand, positive gross margin, replicability, and documented evidence gaps.

use_cases.title: Build a Market Brief
use_cases.description: Convert policies, public transactions, company disclosures, and cases into a sourced maturity and competitive landscape briefing.

prompt_templates.title: Map the Market
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the data element market layers and identify one opportunity in each layer for [industry]. State assumptions and evidence needs.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Business Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [business model] using repeat customers, positive gross margin, and replicability. State evidence gaps and propose a validation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Competitors
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [competitors] by positioning, customers, pricing, strengths, and risks. Separate verified facts from assumptions and date every source.

prompt_templates.title: Size a Strategic Opportunity
prompt_templates.prompt: Estimate TAM, SAM, and SOM for [segment] using two methods. Reconcile differences, document assumptions, and provide sensitivity ranges.

output_examples.input: Assess the current maturity of China's data element market.
output: Stage: transition from model exploration toward scaling.
Signals: established accounting cases, limited transaction volume, early financialization, and emerging public data authorization.
Uncertainty: validate current volumes and policy implementation with dated public sources.

output_examples.input: Evaluate whether a data asset service model is proven.
output: Repeat demand: insufficient evidence until renewal or repeat purchase data is available.
Economics: calculate gross margin after delivery labor, compliance, technology, and partner costs.
Replicability: test delivery effort and conversion across customers or industries.

output_examples.input: Create a market sizing approach for a regional data compliance service.
output: Top-down: narrow total enterprise spending by region, regulated sectors, and addressable service scope.
Bottom-up: multiply qualified customers by annual contract value and realistic penetration.
Cross-check definitions, remove overlapping revenue, and show sensitivity for adoption and pricing.

best_practices: Date every source and distinguish primary evidence, secondary research, and assumptions.
Cross-check market size with top-down and bottom-up methods using consistent definitions.
Separate policy intent from observed transactions, repeat demand, positive margins, and replicable delivery.
anti_patterns: Do not treat policy support, listings, or pilot announcements as proof of commercial demand.
Do not present precise market numbers without scope, date, method, assumptions, and uncertainty.
Do not generalize from successful cases while ignoring failures, selection bias, or implementation barriers.

faq.question: Which markets does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on China's data element market, including resources, products, circulation, services, applications, infrastructure, and emerging financialization.

faq.question: Can it provide current market data?
faq.answer: It can structure current evidence you provide, but it has no live feed. Verify recent facts with dated public sources.

faq.question: How does it assess market maturity?
faq.answer: It reviews policy, transactions, financing, technology, adoption, repeat demand, profitability, and replicability against a four-stage framework.

faq.question: How does it estimate market size?
faq.answer: It combines top-down segmentation with bottom-up customer and contract estimates, then reconciles definitions, overlaps, assumptions, and sensitivity.

faq.question: Can it compare competitors?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares positioning, offerings, customers, cases, pricing models, strengths, weaknesses, and evidence quality.

faq.question: Does it replace professional advice?
faq.answer: No. Legal, regulatory, accounting, financing, and investment decisions require qualified professionals and current authoritative sources.
